Hazard: fnn-owner-core (owner.lisp:578) is a bare fnn-core-state wrapper over *the-live-state*, which the contract gives to the owner section (io.lisp:215-221, 319-336). The progress lambda (bp-node.lisp:1024-1032) runs on the command thread, outside any quantum (bp-session.lisp:195), and calls fnn-bpnode-dispatch-one and its helpers, which read owner state bare (e.g. bp-node.lisp:264 fn-owner-bp-route-table). With a listen port the owner is the served owner (bp-service.lisp:1432) with peer-flight/pull actors that run sections concurrently, so a bare read can race a locked write. The contract row that declared this safe was deleted (e7a8f6ab2) because its stated reason (fnn-owner-core takes the mutex per call) was false and the single-actor alternative is neither stated nor enforced.
fix: Read the state inside a section: wrap the owner-state reads of dispatch-one (route table, receipt detail/observations/result/release/refusal lines, source-decision, request-result-1) in fnn-quantum-bp / fnn-owner-serialized (one quantum per turn, returning the values), or prove and enforce a single-actor invariant for the bp-node owner and then re-declare the callback row with that true reason.
